why: APPEND-ONLY, WRITTEN BY A HUMAN, VERIFIED BY THE BUILD. `fingerprints.json` digests the computed VALUES so a vendor release that changes what a number IS cannot pass unseen — but that defence had one hole, and it was the ordinary workflow: the regeneration is part of taking the release. Install, regenerate, commit, green. Measured, not argued: an inverted-weight `wma`, 2.1% wrong against its own fixture, was planted and the artefacts regenerated the way a release arrives, and every check reported passing. So the digest gets the rule an id already has in renames.json. The generator can see that a number moved; it CANNOT see whether the vendor fixed a defect or shipped one, and those two have opposite consequences for every chart drawn from it. It refuses to write until somebody writes which, here. Nothing is ever deleted from this list: the chain from an indicator's first digest to its current one is how a reader knows what its numbers have been through.
form: Each entry is one indicator moving once: `id`, `from` (the digest on file), `to` (the digest this run derives), `reason` (what changed and how it was confirmed — a sentence, not `vendor update`), and `settles` when the retroactive window moved with it. Entries for one id chain: each `from` is the `to` of the one before it.
